narrative: OMX30 enters Monday with constructive European support: DAX, CAC, and FTSE all positive overnight, establishing a +0.4% to +0.6% tailwind. The index sits in a clear bull regime (+8.1% above 200-MA), though technicals show early fatigue—MACD has rolled below signal, RSI 54.86 is neutral, and ADX at 14.6 reflects weak directional conviction. Gold's +1.90% surge benefits Boliden directly, while the sharp US 10Y yield rise (+89bps) is a double-edged sword: positive for bank NIMs (SEB, Handelsbanken, Swedbank) but compresses tech/telecom DCF valuations. VIX plunge to 15.13 suggests risk-on sentiment, yet escalating trade war rhetoric (Trump-Canada tensions, Iran D-Day economics) creates tactical volatility risk. Entry should target 3123 support; resistance at 3180 (50-MA) and 3200 are key profit-taking zones.
morningBrief: OMX30 setup is moderately bullish but tactically cautious. European strength (+0.4%–+0.6% beta) and gold rally (+1.90%) provide initial upside bias, but MACD roll-under and weak ADX (14.6) signal consolidation rather than explosive move. Watch 3123 (yesterday's close) as immediate pivot; break above 3180 (50-MA) needed to confirm momentum. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) are core longs on the 89bp 10Y yield spike—NIM expansion outweighs rate sensitivity. Boliden gets tailwind from gold and copper firmness; position this as the sector barometer. Avoid early chasing in Ericsson/Hexagon (NASDAQ still soft at +0.43%; tech sentiment fragile). Trade war noise (FT headlines on Trump-Canada, Iran) could trigger 1–2% flash corrections intraday; use dips to add into quality industrials (Volvo, Atlas Copco). Stop-loss discipline below 3085 (lower Bollinger band). US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—watch for recession signal that could flip risk sentiment fast.
